environment: Testnet: Cloudflare Worker mayarin-dashboard-testnet, Railway dashboard-api, zone mayarin.xyz
incident: Every /api/* call from the deployed dashboard answered 403 with a Cloudflare HTML page
symptom: Browser reported "Invalid JSON response". Pages rendered normally, so the deployment looked healthy.
rootCause: The Worker was bound by a zone route, so it ran inside mayarin.xyz's routing. Its subrequests to api-merchant-testnet.mayarin.xyz — another proxied hostname in the same zone — looped back into that routing and Cloudflare refused them. The /api/* proxy returned that response verbatim.
whatItAffected: Every /api/* call, including POST /auth/login — not only the new registration routes
The SSR session check in middleware.ts, so locals.user was always undefined and every protected page redirected to /login
Effect: the testnet dashboard could render but could not be signed in to

introduced.why: The dashboard moved from Pages to a Worker in #252. A Worker custom domain was refused because dashboard-testnet.mayarin.xyz still held a CNAME to the retired mayarin-dashboard-testnet.pages.dev project, so a zone route was used instead — correct-looking, no DNS change, no downtime, and the loopback was not visible.

detected.how: First real use of /register on the deployed testnet dashboard. The evening's work had all been against localhost, so nothing had exercised /api/* on testnet for two days.

diagnosis.decisive: wrangler tail showed the Worker itself returning Ok for the same requests that answered 403
diagnosis.reasoning: A Worker that runs and reports Ok cannot be the thing being blocked, so the 403 had to come from its own subrequest rather than from the route, a WAF rule, or bot filtering
ruledOut: Bot filtering — a browser User-Agent and Referer changed nothing
The new registration code — POST /auth/login failed identically
The API itself — direct calls to api-merchant-testnet.mayarin.xyz answered 200/400 JSON throughout

fixes.change: Pointed API_URL at Railway's own hostname, outside the zone, to escape the loopback
fixes.cost: Left Cloudflare's network on every request, and broke a rule docs/deployment.md states explicitly: do not replace the custom API hostname with Railway's generated one

fixes.change: Bound the Worker by custom_domain instead of a zone route, then returned API_URL to api-merchant-testnet.mayarin.xyz
fixes.prerequisite: The retired Pages CNAME had to be deleted by hand in the Cloudflare dashboard — Cloudflare refuses a custom domain on a hostname holding a hand-managed record (error 100117), and wrangler's OAuth token carries zone (read) only

measurements.method: curl TTFB from one laptop, 3-6 samples per row, warm
measurements.note: A page request carrying a session cookie forces the SSR auth fetch; without one no subrequest is made, which is why the two page rows differ
measurements.conclusion: Proxied API calls are roughly three times faster. No improvement is claimed for the SSR page path: its spread is too wide to read as a change.

surprises: For about a minute after the custom domain was created, requests reached no Worker at all: /login answered 200 from the previous deployment while /register and /verify answered 404, because those pages did not exist in it. wrangler tail was silent throughout, which is how it was told apart from a bad build. It resolved itself with no redeploy.

The first deploy attempt failed with "Successful trigger changes were not rolled back". The site stayed up — the zone route was never detached — but that message is a reason to check the live surface immediately rather than trust the failure.
limitations: Latency measured from one machine on one network; the numbers are a before/after comparison, not an SLO
The 1003 loopback was reproduced and fixed, not proven from Cloudflare's side — no Cloudflare support ticket was raised
No registration was completed end to end on testnet, so the verification email has not been seen in a real inbox
openFollowUps: Sign up through /register on testnet and confirm the code arrives from "Mayarin <notification@send.mayarin.xyz>"
api-testnet.mayarin.xyz and the pay proxy were never affected: pay-proxy has always been bound by custom_domain. Any future Worker on this zone should be too.
